title: Skyline Snack Dash
premise: A cheerful arcade endless runner where a scarf-wearing dog dashes across a skyline route, jumping over street hazards and collecting floating snacks for points.
interaction_model: Single-button endless runner; tap/click anywhere in the playfield or press Space to jump while grounded, with start and restart buttons for run flow.
objective: Collect as many snacks as possible while avoiding any collision with ground obstacles, which immediately ends the run.
progression: Endless score chase with gradual difficulty escalation as each collected snack slightly increases movement speed and spawn pressure.
theme: Playful urban rooftop/street dash with cartoon pet energy and bright arcade styling.
mood: Light, upbeat, snack-chasing, colorful, and slightly hectic as speed increases.
likely_audience: Casual web and mobile players, especially players who enjoy simple one-tap arcade runners and kid-friendly pet-themed games.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is an endless runner built around jump timing, hazard avoidance, and collectible pickup scoring.
Medium confidence on exact fiction details because some hidden placeholder asset labels mention dog, bone, and hydrant while on-screen copy uses skyline/snack/crate language.
High confidence that progression is endless rather than stage-based because there are no levels, checkpoints, or win conditions in code.
High confidence that mobile-first usability was intended due to pointer input, touch-action handling, safe-area aware HUD, and full-screen responsive canvas.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen HTML5 canvas arcade game called \"Skyline Snack Dash\" in which a cute cartoon dog wearing a scarf runs automatically from left to right through a glowing city skyline while the world scrolls toward the player. The player should use one-tap or spacebar controls to make the dog jump only when grounded. Spawn ground hazards such as crates or hydrant-like blockers that cause instant game over on contact, and also spawn floating snack or bone pickups at varying jump heights that increase the score when collected. Make the core loop an endless runner score chase: dodge hazards, time jumps, collect snacks, and survive as long as possible. Each collected snack should slightly increase overall run speed so the game becomes more intense over time. Include a full-screen responsive canvas, a start menu, a score HUD, and a game-over screen with final score and restart button. Present the game with bright arcade polish: layered sky gradient, sun glow, drifting clouds, silhouetted skyline buildings with lit windows, a road strip, grassy ground, score pulse feedback, particles on jumps and pickups, a subtle screen shake on failure, upbeat looping background music, and distinct jump, land, collect, fail, and UI sounds. The tone should feel playful, energetic, and mobile-friendly, with big rounded buttons, bold display typography, and an inviting casual-runner style.
